fatal_errors: The proposed 5-or-more-element applicability range excludes the target quaternary TaVCrW alloy.
The central replacement of thermodynamic integration by MTP-to-DFT free-energy perturbation is omitted.
No quantitative prediction is given for the expected sub-0.5 meV/atom free-energy agreement, 80% resource saving, or approximately 20-fold speedup.
The cited evidence does not establish the claimed elemental or binary free-energy performance of the method.
explanation: The hypothesis correctly identifies the core deficiency of EAM references and proposes an ML interatomic potential with richer many-body descriptors to improve overlap with ab initio liquid configurations. It also recognizes TOR-TILD with EAM references as the baseline and appropriately notes training-set coverage as a limitation. However, it reconstructs only part of the target method: the target specifically uses an MTP with very low fitting error and exploits the resulting small MTP–DFT energy-difference variance to replace expensive TI with rapidly convergent FEP. The response instead retains TI and discusses only a less quantitative reduction in path mismatch. Its stated domain is also inconsistent with the quaternary BCC TaVCrW target, and it omits the 2000–2400 K range, 0 GPa condition, 3456-atom cell, and PBE/LDA calculations. Important physical contributions from electronic excitations and solid-state SRO are absent, as are the reported computational savings and melting-point shifts. The proposed comparison is directionally useful but lacks the decisive benchmark of FEP against TI, preferably on VW, with an explicit agreement threshold of 0.5 meV/atom. Finally, E1 concerns broad HEA phase stability and E2 only gives generic support for ML potentials; neither supplies the asserted elemental or binary validation.
